body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, October 8, and the day's biggest story is the Kern River case that reached the California Supreme Court this week, where justices heard arguments over how the state balances fish and water supplies. Expect another hot one — a high near 100 degrees, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County this morning.

## The Kern Overnight

Firefighters spent the small hours at the old Silver Saddle Ranch & Club in California City, where a second-alarm fire broke out just after 12:30 a.m. at the two-story hotel resort. Crews arrived to find three buildings fully involved, an exposure threatened to the east, and four spot fires in vegetation to the south backing into the wind. The only hydrant on scene was dead, so a water tender was called in along with support from Edwards. Firefighters kept the flames out of the main exposure and turned their attention to a smaller on-site building, while roughly an acre to an acre and a half of grass and brush burned around the complex. The initial fire buildings were reported 100 percent involved, and crews settled in for an extensive mop-up as light southwest winds turned erratic on one side of the fire.

Elsewhere, a semi caught fire on Interstate 5 near Copus Road, south of the Grapevine, with the trailer still attached. Crews reported the fire near the wheel wells before the whole trailer went up in heavy smoke, blocking lanes and routing traffic off the freeway onto Highway 99 while heavy towing was called in. One lane was expected to reopen within about ten minutes, and the ambulance was cancelled with no one hurt.

In south Bakersfield, a hysterical caller reported that two men and a woman forced entry through the front door of an apartment in the 7000 block of Di Giorgio Road. Officers searched the unit and the surrounding area while medics staged nearby. Deputies also were sent to the North Edwards area for a man in a black shirt and gray sweatpants standing in the middle of a roadway with a large firearm, possibly a rifle or shotgun; the caller, who was picking up juveniles from a school event, told dispatchers she left with them and filed a report. And a caller reported a man in an orange Chevrolet pickup dragging a woman from a residence in the 1800 block of Pacific Street, with the woman heard yelling as she was put into the truck before the vehicle left the area. The rest of the night was crashes, disturbances, alarms and medical aids.

## Today's weather

It's 79 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 100 and a low around 69 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires reported. Air quality sits at 83, which is moderate — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a reasonable day to keep the strenuous outdoor work to the cooler hours. With the valley running this hot in October, keep the water handy and check on neighbors who work outside.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Ridgecrest's police chief says the city is amending its Flock camera contract in response to resident pushback and concerns.** The license-plate-reading cameras have drawn questions from residents about privacy and how the data is stored and shared, and the city is now reworking the terms of its agreement rather than leaving it as written. It's a local version of a debate playing out across California, and it matters here because Ridgecrest is far from the nearest big-city police force — the cameras are part of how a smaller department stretches its coverage.

**According to KGET 17, a vanload of Central Valley farm workers was reportedly picked up by ICE.** Details remain limited, but the report lands in the middle of a harvest season that depends on this workforce, and it's the kind of thing that ripples through families and employers well beyond the people directly involved. We'll keep watching for more information as it comes.

**KGET 17 also reports that the Bakersfield City Council approved an $8 million contract for energy savings construction at the Water Resources building.** The work is pitched as efficiency upgrades that pay for themselves over time, and the council's vote moves it from proposal to project. For ratepayers, the practical question is whether the savings show up where they should — in the cost of running the department.

**23ABC reports that the California Supreme Court heard arguments Wednesday in Bring Back the Kern v. City of Bakersfield, a case that could reshape how the state balances protecting fish in the Kern River with other water needs.** The dispute centers on a state law requiring enough water below dams to keep fish in good condition; in 2023 a judge ordered Bakersfield to keep water flowing in the river, the city and several agricultural water districts challenged that order, and an appeals court overturned the original ruling, sending the matter to the state's highest court. The city declined to comment on active litigation, and the City Attorney's Office did not respond to 23ABC's request. As arguments unfolded, Bring Back the Kern hosted a watch party at Dagny's Coffee Co. so residents could follow along together. Gary Bray, president of the Kern River Fly Fishing Club, told 23ABC there has to be a way to allow water for drinking, for communities and for agriculture — "we need both." Isabel Stierle, a retired Bakersfield College biology professor, said how we treat the natural setting reflects how we treat each other, and that we need to think about keeping things alive and keeping the river flowing.

**23ABC reports that a $2 million state investment is bringing a new resource center closer to opening for Delano farmworkers.** Senator Melissa Hurtado secured the funding for the California Farmworker Foundation, capping a two-year effort that organizers first unveiled in June. The center is meant to be a central hub where farmworker families can reach healthcare and support services more easily. Foundation CEO Darrell Muniz described it as a safe and trusted place where farmworkers feel seen, heard and empowered — where a mother can get care for her family, a father can learn a skill, and a child can believe they can do anything. Farmer Melvin Archila, a member of the foundation's Agricultural Work Advisory Council, said the foundation has opened doors for him in his work and his leadership.

**23ABC reports that two courthouse break-ins are under investigation in Bakersfield, and a 20-year-old man is in custody after allegedly forcing his way into the Kern County Superior Courthouse.** Keenean Miranda was arrested after allegedly making his way to the sixth floor, where officials apprehended him; he faces four counts, including assault with a deadly weapon and first- and second-degree burglary. A separate break-in on Sept. 23 targeted the office of Kern County Superior Court Judge David Zulfa — police have not confirmed whether anything was taken, and no arrests have been announced in that case. Bakersfield Police Sergeant Keith Schlecht told 23ABC the courthouse incidents are among nine offenses downtown, ranging from simple vandalism to burglaries where entry was made and theft committed, with six suspects identified and five arrests made.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man accused of using a stolen credit card for more than $1,000 in purchases.** Investigators are asking the public to help identify him. If you think you recognize something, call BPD's non-emergency line rather than the newsroom — and never post a name or plate on social media.

## Something good

The Kern County Veterans Stand Down returns for its annual event at Stramler Park, offering support and services to local veterans. It's one of those gatherings where the paperwork, the health checks and the conversation all happen in one place, and volunteers show up year after year to make it work. If you know a veteran who could use a hand, this is a good week to pass the word along.

## Coming up this week

Today, Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon. Friday brings two noon meetings — the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee — so if you've had thoughts about a blighted lot or a neighborhood concern, that's your window.

Monday is busy: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m. Tuesday, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon — a good room for anyone with opinions about bike lanes, crosswalks or traffic calming. Wednesday, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m., which lands just days after the Kern River arguments in Sacramento, so expect the case to come up. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 15, at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off on Friday, FANTASIAS on Saturday, United We Dance on Oct. 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on Oct. 17, and Fortune Feimster's Taking Care of Biscuits comedy tour on Oct. 18. Have a good Thursday, and stay cool out there.

top.title: Ridgecrest police chief says city is amending Flock camera contract based on resident pushback, concerns
